name: lockstep
concept: An intelligent credential adversary that first fingerprints lab hosts to build a live auth-surface map (SSH, FTP, web login forms, SMTP, MySQL/Postgres), then synthesizes small context-aware likely-credential dictionaries from service banners, hostnames, default creds, and tiny curated wordlists, and finally sprays them with lockout-safe adaptive pacing, per-account cooldown, and response-learned session hygiene so each guess learns from service-coded responses instead of brute force. Stacks default-credential checks against common lab frameworks (Tomcat, Jenkins, routers, DVWA, WordPress, postgres) as a first pass.
attack_vectors: context-derived dictionary construction from hostnames, banners, and small curated wordlists
lockout-aware adaptive credential spraying with per-account exponential backoff and response fingerprinting
default-credential checks against known lab frameworks and appliances
dictionary priority from service-specific likelihood models
novelty_angle: Intelligence beats breadth: it builds dictionaries from the target's own fingerprints and paces itself around lockout thresholds, making it a credential adversary that reasons about response codes and lock state — a context-to-credential inference engine rather than a bulk sprayer.
dependencies: stdlib (socket, http, smtp, imap, ssl) for SMTP/IMAP/web/FTP
allowlist hosts file / CIDR parsing validated against scope
scope_gate: Only accepts targets matching the lab allowlist (loopback, RFC1918 private ranges, user-supplied lab CIDR); out-of-allowlist host refused at plan time before any connection; WARN banner on first run; hard stop if allowlist missing or --lab-cidr absent.
